header:
Date: 2026-08-02 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Carter (Verdant Head of Security), Elena Ruiz (Verdant VP Legal), Marcus Lee (Verdant CTO)
summary: Call to review MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing approval for Dedicated capacity, and vendor onboarding checklist. Customer flagged data residency and encryption/KMS as blockers; legal requested updated MSA with indemnity and data processing terms. Redwood to share SOC2 and pen test artifacts and prepare benchmark plan for Dedicated vs Hosted. Agreed next steps and timeline toward signoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan Meyers from Redwood, I am the AE on this. Priya from our infra team will cover technical and benchmarks.
[00:07] Priya: hi all, thanks, excited to dig in.
[00:10] Liam: Hey - Liam Carter here, head of security at Verdant. We have Elena and Marcus as well.
[00:15] Elena: hi all.
[00:18] Marcus: hello.
[00:22] Jordan: Quick agenda - legal redlines to the MSA/DPA, confirm SLAs / SLOs for Dedicated plan, pricing approvals and onboarding steps. We'll also cover security docs and benchmarking. Anything to add?
[00:31] Elena: No, that covers it. We need to close on indemnity language and the data processing terms - specifically around subprocessor lists and audit rights.
[00:40] Liam: And data residency - we can't have certain patient records leave EU.
[00:45] Priya: We support VPC deployments and on-prem options; for Hosted we have regional deployments in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. For Dedicated we can also put a cluster in their preferred region, but there are lead times.
[00:58] Marcus: Lead times? What are we talking about, weeks or months?
[01:02] Priya: Typically provisioning Dedicated capacity is 2-4 weeks once contracts are signed and we have network connectivity - if there's special on-prem packaging it could be longer. There are also warm-up tasks for model weights and kernel tuning.
[01:15] Elena: Understood. On the MSA we redlined section 7.2 around indemnity and 11.4 around data breach notification timelines - our legal counsel wants 48 hours for notification.
[01:27] Jordan: OK the 48 hour ask - our standard is 72 for incident acknowledgement and 30 days for detailed forensics, but we can discuss narrowing the acknowledgement window. Let me hand to Priya for security posture details that might help.
[01:37] Priya: Sure - we have SOC 2 Type II, annual pen tests, and we can supply the pen test summary. For encryption, data at rest is AES-256; keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM for Private deployments. Hosted customers can request CMK via supported cloud KMS, and we log key usage to audit logs.
[01:55] Liam: Are audit logs immutable and retained for - what's the retention?
[02:00] Priya: Default retention is 90 days in the console; we offer extended retention packages. Logs are append-only in our storage backend, and we can ship to customer SIEM via secure S3 or syslog.
[02:09] Elena: We also need proof that subprocessors are contractually bound - can you provide your subprocessor list and dates?
[02:15] Jordan: Yes, we'll share the current subprocessor list; it's included in our security pack. We'll also mark any planned changes.
[02:21] Marcus: Pricing side - our procurement needs committed cost for Dedicated for budgeting; what's the ballpark for the cluster we discussed (4x A100-ish nodes)?
[02:30] Jordan: For the configuration we discussed, committed monthly reserved capacity is around $65k-$90k depending on quantization and model family; price breaks for 12-24 month commits. We can provide a precise quote after we finalize expected QPS and token volumes.
[02:45] Marcus: Okay procurement wants that in writing for next Tuesday.
[02:48] Jordan: We'll get that quote over.
[02:50] Elena: On the DPA side, data deletion and retention - we need specifics about backups and backups retention and guaranteed wipe.
[02:58] Priya: For Dedicated, snapshots are stored in customer-owned buckets if requested; otherwise in our compartment with life-cycle policies. We support secure deletion and can provide certificate of destruction on decommission. For Hosted, we retain model KV caches for a short prefix window - but PII should not be stored in prompts; we recommend prompt redaction and tokenization.
[03:18] Liam: We need to run a limited benchmark to validate latency SLOs - our app needs 95th pct under 250ms for short chats and batch embeddings at X throughput.
[03:28] Priya: Sounds good - our SE team can run a dedicated benchmark: we'll test 95th percentile latency at configured concurrency and share traces. We need representative prompt sets and target QPS from you.
[03:38] Marcus: I'll have engineering provide those.
[03:40] Jordan: Great. Elena, are there any MSA redlines beyond indemnity and breach timelines?
[03:46] Elena: We edited 9.3 on liability caps and want to carve out gross negligence and willful misconduct. We also asked for SOC2 and pen test artifacts; the DPA redlines include data residency and subprocessors plus audit rights.
[04:00] Jordan: Understood. On liability caps, we can discuss carve-outs - I'll flag to our legal ops. We typically have a liability cap of fees paid over prior 12 months.
[04:10] Elena: That won't fly for us without carve-outs.
[04:13] Jordan: Noted. I'll escalate.
[04:16] Priya: For the security team, if it helps, we can do a security workshop or a live pen test window where we review findings together - that sometimes accelerates approvals.
[04:27] Liam: That could help. Also need to confirm SSO/SAML integration options and RBAC.
[04:33] Priya: We support SAML SSO via SSO providers; RBAC is per-route and token-level. We can map your groups to roles and export logs for access.
[04:42] Marcus: About onboarding - what does the timeline look like from signature to production? We have a launch window in Sept.
[04:49] Jordan: If contracts signed early August and no major legal blockers, Dedicated provisioning mid-August and a 2-3 week integration window could hit early Sept. If you need earlier, Hosted + VPC peering is fastest to start pilot.
[05:03] Elena: We prefer Dedicated but fine to start pilot on Hosted while we finalize MSA.
[05:09] Jordan: Good plan. Pricing approval - Elena, Marcus, will procurement sign off with the quote?
[05:14] Marcus: Procurement needs the finalized quote and the MSA redlines resolved; they also asked for pricing hold for 30 days.
[05:21] Jordan: We can hold pricing for 30 days upon issuing the quote.
[05:25] Liam: A couple of technical clarifications: do you support bring-your-own-models (BYOM) or only model catalog?
[05:32] Priya: For Dedicated and Private we support BYOM in most cases; for Hosted we host curated models but we can do custom model onboarding under an advanced agreement. Models requiring special kernels or licensing may add time.
[05:43] Marcus: For our inference pattern, we do long-context summarization and some embeddings for search; we care about KV cache persistence between sessions. Is that supported?
[05:52] Priya: Yes, persistent KV cache for session state is supported in Dedicated; we manage cache tiering and eviction policies and can snapshot caches on schedule. For Hosted, ephemeral caches are the default but we have managed cache options.
[06:05] Elena: Back to DPA - who is the data controller/processor in your wording? We need explicit language.
[06:10] Jordan: In the DPA we designate the customer as controller and Redwood as processor by default; we'll send the sample.
[06:16] Elena: Good. Also please indicate subprocessors and subprocessor fallback.
[06:20] Jordan: Will do.
[06:22] [System note: brief audio glitch]
[06:25] Priya: Also note quantization options - we can suggest int8 to lower cost which affects latency and some perf tradeoffs. We'll include recommended quant and perf notes in the benchmark plan.
[06:37] Liam: For security review, does Redwood allow a right-to-audit clause or do you provide audit reports only?
[06:43] Jordan: We provide SOC2 reports and pen test summaries; full on-site audits are handled case-by-case - usually through a secure audit process under NDA.
[06:52] Elena: That should be fine. Marcus, anything else from engineering?
[06:56] Marcus: One ask - we want explicit SLA terms for model availability and failover. If Dedicated cluster has issues, what's the failover path?
[07:04] Priya: We maintain automated failover to a warm standby in the region for Dedicated clusters with cross-zone replication. For critical SLAs we can propose an elevated SLA with a higher uptime target and specific remediation credits spelled out in the SLR. We'll include example SLA language in the follow-up.
[07:19] Marcus: Also what's the RTO for KV cache loss?
[07:22] Priya: Depends on config - with persistent cache snapshots we can restore within hours; if ephemeral there's potential cold-start impacts. We'll recommend snapshot cadence for your workload.
[07:31] Jordan: OK I want to confirm deliverables: Jordan will send MSA redlines and updated DPA sample, SOC2 and pen test artifacts, subprocessor list, and pricing quote. Priya will put together a benchmark plan and template tests. Customer will supply representative prompt sets, target QPS, and legal redlines.
[07:47] Elena: Yes. We also want a proposed SLA paragraph with uptime and credits.
[07:52] Jordan: We'll add that.
[07:54] Liam: One more item - encryption key lifecycle for CMK: who has rotation control and can we map to our KMS policies?
[08:02] Priya: For customer-managed keys we can integrate with your KMS; rotation policies controlled by you. For hosted CMK there is a shared control model but we can provide key usage logs.
[08:12] Elena: Great. On timelines: we'll aim to get legal redlines back within three business days.
[08:16] Jordan: Sounds good - so action items and next call - can we target Aug 9 for legal signoff meeting?
[08:21] Elena: Aug 9 works provisionally.
[08:23] Marcus: Good.
[08:24] Jordan: Perfect - thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the doc pack and quote.
[08:29] Elena: Thanks.
[08:31] Liam: Thanks.
[08:32] [Call ends]

Notes: Transcription contains a few minor mis-hearings (e.g., kernel vs kernel tuning sometimes transcripted as "carrel tuning"). References to product names: Dedicated, Hosted, Private, KV cache, CMK, KMS, SOC2.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Jordan: Send MSA/DPA redlines + SOC2 + pen test summary + subprocessor list + pricing quote (by 2026-08-05).
- Priya: Share benchmark plan and tests (by 2026-08-06).
- Verdant: Provide prompt sets, target QPS, and legal redlines (by 2026-08-04).
- Schedule final legal review on 2026-08-09.

End of transcript.
